+def _apply_table(s, table):
+    """
+    s.replace(ps, c) for every (ps, c) in table, in order. Replacements whose
+    pair holds a code point absent from s are skipped (they cannot match):
+    present is a superset of the code points of s (minted tokens are added
+    whenever a replacement changed s, nothing is ever removed).
+    """
+    present = set(s)
+    add = present.add
+    n = len(s)
+    for ps, c in table:
+        if ps[0] in present and ps[1] in present:
+            s = s.replace(ps, c)
+            m = len(s)
+            if m != n:
+                n = m
+                add(c)
+    return s

+def _split_special(text, special):
+    """
+    Same parts as re.split("(" + "|".join(map(re.escape, special)) + ")", text)
+    minus the empty strings: the leftmost occurrence of any special token is
+    split off, and at equal positions the first one in dict order wins (like
+    the regex alternation). Empty special tokens fall back to the regex.
+    """
+    toks = list(special)
+    if not all(toks):
+        pattern = "(" + "|".join(re.escape(k) for k in toks) + ")"
+        return re.split(pattern, text)
+    find = text.find
+    nxt = [find(k) for k in toks]
+    parts = []
+    app = parts.append
+    pos = 0
+    while True:
+        best = -1
+        bi = -1
+        for i, j in enumerate(nxt):
+            if j >= 0 and (best < 0 or j < best):
+                best = j
+                bi = i
+        if best < 0:
+            break
+        tok = toks[bi]
+        if best > pos:
+            app(text[pos:best])
+        app(tok)
+        pos = best + len(tok)
+        # refresh the occurrences that start before the new position
+        for i, j in enumerate(nxt):
+            if 0 <= j < pos:
+                nxt[i] = find(toks[i], pos)
+    if pos < len(text):
+        app(text[pos:])
+    return parts
+

journal.text:
I worked on encode performance in minbpe after reading lineage_bench.py, basic.py, regex.py and base.py. I edited the merge loop area in basic.py and several spots in regex.py, including the pattern line at 18, the encode path around 311, and a 40-line insertion near line 35. Some edits were reverted and redone.

I ran one sandbox evaluation on encode_ir. Build and equivalence were fine, with identical outputs, but it was rejected for no improvement. encode_ir went from 420012634 to 424860522, ratio 1.0115, against a required 0.9900. train_ir also got slightly worse, 366041664 to 366749050, ratio 1.0019. I stopped without submitting a candidate.

My changes added overhead instead of removing it. The encode hot path is not where my edits were helping, and extra setup code near the top of regex.py likely cost more than it saved.

Next time I should profile encode first, find the dominant cost in the per-chunk merge loop, and make one small targeted change at a time before stacking edits.
